extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and journalists interested in media ownership, political-economy of news, and news-selection effects
extracted.subtask_short: media ownership effects on news selection
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and operationalize Ben Bagdikian's documented mechanisms and patterns by which ownership concentration shapes news selection in US mass media, including testable predictions for content-analysis research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conglomerate Cross-Interest Suppression
rubrics_metrics.description: When a media company is part of a conglomerate, news critical of any subsidiary's business is suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bagdikian documents specific cases of suppressed stories; implies a structural disincentive to publish reporting that would harm other corporate holdings. Useful as a hypothesis for cross-outlet comparative content analysis (compare coverage of parent-subsidiary misconduct vs competitors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertiser Sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrated outlets dependent on a smaller number of major advertisers face stronger pressure to avoid stories that would alienate them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertiser relationships shape editorial choices; outlets targeting advertiser-friendly topics get preference. Use advertiser composition as a covariate when testing coverage biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-Averse Editorial Culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Large publicly-traded media companies face shareholder pressure for predictable revenue; controversial coverage that risks subscriber/advertiser loss is demoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shareholder-driven emphasis on predictable revenue creates editorial conservatism and reduces willingness to run high-risk investigative or adversarial stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underreporting of Corporate Misbehavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-ownership creates structural disincentive to investigate corporate practices similar to those of the parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect lower incidence/intensity of reporting on corporate wrongdoing when the subject is linked to the owner's corporate interests; testable against coverage of equivalent misconduct by unaffiliated firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underreporting of Labor Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Major media owned by anti-union conglomerates underreport labor stories favorable to workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage of strikes, union organizing, and labor-management conflict will be muted or framed unfavorably when ownership is anti-union; compare tone and placement across ownership types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underreporting of Media Industry Itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Press criticism of media practices (concentration, monopoly) is systematically thin in mainstream outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that critically examine media ownership or industry consolidation are underrepresented in outlets owned by large conglomerates; raises conflicts-of-interest concerns for media self-coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro-Advertiser Topic Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics congenial to major advertiser categories (cars, pharma, finance) get extensive coverage, often favorable; topics critical of those industries get less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic-frequency skew toward advertiser-favored beats; expect both selection and tonal bias (favorable framing) for advertiser-relevant topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideological Convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrated ownership produces editorial-line convergence; divergent perspectives are squeezed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After consolidation or acquisition, editorial positions across formerly diverse outlets tend to standardize; measure via longitudinal tone/position analysis across outlets sharing ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Resource Depletion
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost-cutting under concentrated ownership shrinks investigative units; investigative stories therefore decline in frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative output is proportional to investigative budgets, which are reduced under consolidation; operationalize by comparing investigative staffing/budget and story counts pre/post consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affluent-Audience Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisers' demand for affluent audiences shapes editorial selection so that stories appealing to affluent readers are over-supplied and those appealing to lower-income readers are under-supplied at the front-page level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manifestations include: oversupply of luxury consumer goods, financial markets, investment topics; under-supply of food prices, housing, public services; redesigning newspapers to emphasize advertiser-targeted sections; treating low-purchasing-power audiences as commercially uninteresting. Use audience demographic targeting and section placement as variables when assessing coverage bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate-Subsidiary Story Suppression (Operational Prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of business misconduct by a conglomerate's subsidiaries is less than coverage of equivalent misconduct by competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testable prediction for content analysis: control for story severity and compare incidence and prominence between affiliated vs unaffiliated firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affluent-Audience Topic Premium (Operational Prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifestyle, financial, investment, real estate, and consumer-electronics topics are over-represented relative to general-audience interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predict over-representation of advertiser-friendly beats; operationalize by comparing topic distributions to audience-interest baselines or population-level relevance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertiser-Friendly Headline Tone (Operational Prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines on advertiser-industry topics skew toward neutral or positive even when underlying findings are negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure headline tone vs article content sentiment for advertiser-relevant topics; expect systematic headline softening or dilution of negative implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative-Cost Constraint (Operational Prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigative outputs are proportional to investigative budget, which shrinks under concentrated ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize by linking investigative story counts/length/depth to documented investigative staffing and budget levels across ownership regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial-Line Standardization (Operational Prediction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial positions across owned outlets converge over time following acquisition or consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test via longitudinal comparisons of editorial endorsements, op-ed slant, or editorial-stance coding before and after ownership changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership as Covariate in News-Selection Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership should be used as a predictor variable in modern news-selection studies because Bagdikian's work shows ownership affects selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers are advised to include outlet ownership as an explanatory covariate when modeling topic selection, tone, investigative output, and placement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability/Testability of Story-Suppression Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories most under-covered should be those threatening parent companies' interests; this is a testable hypothesis on cross-outlet content data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational tests: identify stories that would threaten parent interests and measure relative coverage across outlets with and without those parent ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizability of Ownership Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership data are public and effects on coverage are measurable via topic-frequency analysis and related content measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages empirical implementation: gather public ownership records, construct ownership-linked outlet groups, and apply topic/tone/placement analyses to measure hypothesized effects.
